text: Surendrapuri is significant in three ways: (1) as India's first mythological theme park, providing an educational and devotional experience of Hindu epics, Puranas, and Saptalokas through 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway; (2) as a religious-tourism destination housing multiple temples, including the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (with a 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman from Kanchi and a Mahashivalinga similar to the Pasupatinath in Nepal), 9 Navagraha Temples (each planet with its consort and vahana), and the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga; and (3) as a 'tirth yatra' in a single place — visitors can see life-size replicas of 100+ of India's most famous temples in one visit. It is highly relevant for planetary dosha remedies (Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha, Kaalasarpa Dosha at Nagakoti; planetary shanti at Navagraha Temples) and for protective worship (Panchamukha Hanuman). It is usually visited in conjunction with the famous Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away), forming a popular weekend pilgrimage from Hyderabad.

text: Devotees believe that the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman at the temple protects them from evil and grants courage. The Panchamukha avatara is especially worshipped for protection from black magic, evil eye, and negative energies (since Hanuman, in this form, killed the 5 bees that hid Mahi Ravan's life — defeating all 5 forms of evil simultaneously). The 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga, encircled by Kaalasarpa, is believed to be so powerful that just by pradakshina (circumambulation) one can attain salvation from the ill-effects of Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha and Kaalasarpa Dosha. The 9 Navagraha Temples are believed to mitigate the negative effects of planetary positions on a devotee's horoscope. The 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas at Nagakoti are believed to carry the divine energy of the main 101-foot Shivalinga. Many devotees also visit Surendrapuri as a comprehensive 'temple tour of India' — a unique way to gain familiarity with India's diverse temple architecture and mythology in a single visit.

text: Surendrapuri is built across 17 acres of land, with a 3-km pathway marked by arrows that visitors follow in sequence. The architecture is a unique blend of devotional art, museum display, and temple construction. The complex is divided into multiple zones: (1) The 3-km main pathway inside the Kaladhamam (mythological museum) housing 3,000+ sculptures in 4 categories (Temples of India, Epics of India, Puranas, Saptalokas) — some open air, some indoor depending on size and scene; (2) The Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam — a Vaastu- and Agama-compliant temple with North-South blended Gopuras, housing the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman (black stone from Kanchi) and the Mahashivalinga; (3) The 9 Navagraha Temples — each painted in the colour of the principal deity, with the Navagraha, its consort, and vahana installed; (4) The 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga atop Nagadri Hill, encircled by Kaalasarpa with 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas; (5) The 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance. Descriptions in Telugu and English accompany every exhibit, making the complex accessible to all.

text: Traditional and modest attire is recommended. Per general Telugu temple convention, men often wear dhoti (and may remove the shirt at the inner sanctums); women wear sarees or salwar suits. text: October to March is the most pleasant weather window. Special days: Hanuman Jayanti (March/April), Maha Shivaratri (Feb/March), and weekends (especially Sundays). For the most comfortable experience, visit on a weekday morning. The 3-km pathway takes 2–3 hours to walk through completely; plan for at least half a day. Carry water and an umbrella, as much of the pathway is open-air. Avoid peak summer (April–June) due to the heat. Most pilgrims combine Surendrapuri with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day trip from Hyderabad.

text: The Panchamukha avatara of Hanuman is itself a miracle: Hanuman manifested this form to kill 5 bees that hid Mahi Ravan's life, saving Ram and Lakshman from his clutches. The Panchamukha Hanuman holds 10 different weapons in his hands and has 5 different faces (Vanara, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagreeva) — a unique protective avatara. The Panchamukha Shiva statue represents the Pancha bhootha and Pancha tatwa — the five elements and the five cosmic principles; his 5 faces are Sadyojatha, Vama deva, Aghora, Tatpurusha and Eeshana. The 60-foot double-sided statue of Panchamukha Hanuman and Shiva at the entrance is one of the tallest religious statues in the Telugu-speaking states. The 101-foot Shivalinga at Nagakoti is one of the tallest Shivalingas in India, encircled by the giant snake Kaalasarpa and accompanied by 10 million small Shivalingas made from anthill mud.

text:
Question: What is Surendrapuri — Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam?
Answer: Surendrapuri is India's first mythological theme park and religious tourism destination, spread over 17 acres in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, at the foothills of Yadagirigutta. Opened in May 2003 by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana (in memory of his son Surendra), the complex features 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway in 4 categories: Temples of India (life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples), Epics of India (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, Buddha Charita), Puranas, and Saptalokas (7 celestial worlds). It also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman + Mahashivalinga), 9 Navagraha Temples, the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga, and a 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance.

text:
Question: Who is the presiding deity of Surendrapuri?
Answer: The presiding deity is the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman (a five-faced protective avatara of Hanuman), carved from black stone specially brought from Kanchi. The Panchamukha Hanuman has 5 faces (Vanara, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagreeva) and holds 10 different weapons. He manifested this form to kill the 5 bees that hid the life of Mahi Ravan (Ravana's brother), saving Ram and Lakshman. Lord Venkateswara and Goddess Lakshmi are also worshipped in the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam complex. The complex also includes a Mahashivalinga of Panchamukha Parameswara (similar to Pasupatinath, Nepal).

text:
Question: What can I see at the Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (Mythological Museum)?
Answer: The 3-km Kaladhamam pathway is divided into 4 categories: (1) Temples of India — life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples including Tirumala Balaji, Madurai Meenakshi, Kashi Viswanath, Shirdi Saibaba, Kolkata Kali, Rameswaram, Jagannath Puri, Golden Temple (Amritsar), Somnath, Kedarnath, Guruvayur, and many more; (2) Epics of India — scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, and Buddha Charita; (3) Puranas — Ksheera Sagara Madhanam (churning of the ocean), Gajendra Moksham, Padmavyuham, Kurukshetra War, Pralayakalam, Shiva-Parvathi Kalyam, etc.; (4) Saptalokas — the 7 celestial worlds (Brahmalok, Vishnulok, Shivalok, Nagalok, Indralok, Yamalok/Narakalok, Patalalok) with audio-visual effects. There are 3,000+ sculptures in total, both open-air and indoor depending on the size of the replica.

text:
Question: What is the Nagakoti?
Answer: The Nagakoti is a 101-foot Shivalinga situated atop the Nagadri Hill, encircled by the giant snake Kaalasarpa, with 10 million small Shivalingas made from anthill mud. It is believed to be so powerful that just by pradakshina (circumambulation) one can attain salvation from the ill-effects of Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha, and Kaalasarpa Dosha. Special pujas (Kalasarpa dosha, Naga dosha, Kuja dosha, Parihara poojalu) are performed here. Open 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM daily.

text:
Question: How much time do I need at Surendrapuri?
Answer: The 3-km Kaladhamam pathway takes 2-3 hours to walk through completely (per Tripadvisor reviews). With the temples (Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara, 9 Navagraha, Nagakoti), plan for at least half a day. Most pilgrims combine Surendrapuri with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day pilgrimage from Hyderabad.

text:
Question: Who founded Surendrapuri?
Answer: Surendrapuri was designed and built by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana, who was born in a small village near Khammam in an agricultural family. The sudden passing away of his youngest son, Surendra Babu, motivated him to build a memorial that would keep his son's memory alive. The park is named after Surendra. At the age of 70, after facing dissuasion from friends and associates, he worked doubly hard to bring his dream project to life. After over a decade of dedicated work, Surendrapuri was opened to the public in May 2003. The Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (the mythological museum) was inaugurated in February 2009 by the then-Governor of Andhra Pradesh, N.D. Tiwari.

text:
Question: What are the special pujas at the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam?
Answer: Special pujas include: (1) Suprabhataseva — early-morning waking ritual; (2) Manyusuktham Sahashodhopachara Puja — special 1008-item offering puja; (3) Panchamutranijabishekam — five-sacred-substance abhishekam; (4) Manyusuktham Parayanam — Vedic hymn recitation. At the Navagraha Temples, special graha-dosha pujas, homas, and Navagraha Homa (eradication of evil) are performed. At Nagakoti, parihara poojas (Kaalasarpa, Naga, Kuja) are performed. text:
Question: Is Surendrapuri suitable for children and families?
Answer: Yes — it's an excellent family destination. Children below 5 years enter free; the Kaladhamam is widely praised as 'a great place to teach kids about Hindu mythology and culture' (per JustDial reviews). The pathway is wheelchair-accessible. However, the 3-km walk can be tiring for young children or elderly visitors — plan to take breaks. The pathway is largely open-air, so bring water and an umbrella. Photography is restricted inside the museum, so don't promise kids they can take photos.

text: Alternate names: Swarnagiri Temple Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple Yadadri Tirumala Devasthanam Swarnagiri Balaji Temple Swarnagiri Venkateswara Swamy Temple Manepally Hills Temple Golden Hill Temple Swarnagiri Sree Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam Alternate spellings: Swarnagiri Swarna Giri Swarnagiri Temple Suvarnagiri Manepally Hills Temple Presiding deity: Lord Sri Venkateswara Swamy (12-foot-tall black-granite idol, gold- and silver-adorned; the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana). The idol is flanked by Goddesses Sridevi and Bhu Devi on either side (per official site image of the sanctum). Other deities: Goddess Padmavati (Alamelu Manga) — consort of Lord Venkateswara Goddess Godadevi Madan Gopal Krishna Swamy Garuda Alwar (vahana of Lord Venkateswara) Sri Ramanujacharya (in his own sub-shrine) Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Lord Bhu Varahaswamy Jala Narayana Swamy (illuminated water-filled sanctum — visual highlight in evenings) Lord Anjaneya Swamy (40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue at the temple; 27-foot Anjaneya as per Telugu Wikipedia) Lord Ganesha (Vinayaka) Vakula Matha Vedic scholars' idols (Veda Murthis) by the pushkarini Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam, also known as Yadadri Tirumala Devasthanam, is a modern Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, located atop the scenic Manepally Hills (Swarnagiri Hills) in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana — about 47 km from Hyderabad. Built by the Manepally family (Manepally Charitable Trust / Srivari Seva Trust) on 22 acres of their own land, construction began in 2018 and the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy, following Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya. The temple features a 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a 27-foot Anjaneya, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest), a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi, multiple sub-shrines (Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi), and 108 steps leading up to the hilltop. Daily footfall is 70,000–80,000 (crossing 1 lakh on festivals). General darshan is free; special darshan tickets start at ₹50. Open 5 AM to 9 PM daily.

text: section: Founder's Family Story & Motivation content: The idea of building Swarnagiri Temple came from a deeply personal miracle in the Manepally family. In 2016, Vijayalaxmi, the wife of Sri Manepally Rama Rao, had a life-threatening accident in an escalator that broke her bones and pushed her into a coma. The doctors gave up. It was the holy water (tirtham) that somebody brought from Tirupati that brought her back to life. The Manepally family, in thanksgiving, decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara — to celebrate the miracle and offer a Tirupati-like spiritual hub closer to Hyderabad. The Manepally family is a prominent jewellery business family from Telangana, led by Sri Manepally Rama Rao (a businessman and philanthropist) along with his two sons, trustees Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi, Manepally Murali Krishna, Manepally Sri Latha, Manepally Gopi Krishna, and Manepally Mamatha. Under the Manepally Charitable Trust (also called the Srivari Seva Trust, established 30 January 2024), the family dedicated approximately 22 acres of prime land on a hillock that overlooks the historic Bhongir landscape. The name 'Swarnagiri' (meaning 'Golden Hill') was chosen to reflect the inner radiance and spiritual wealth the temple aims to bestow. foundation year: Construction began in 2018; temple formally consecrated (Prana Pratishtha + Kumbhabhishekam) on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Sri Sri Sri Chinna Jeeyar Swamy (per the Telugu Wikipedia; some English sources say 7 March 2024 — both dates are close and refer to the consecration festivities). founders: Sri Manepally Rama Rao (businessman and philanthropist; led the temple construction with his two sons; born into a prominent jewellery business family from Telangana) Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi (wife of Sri Manepally Rama Rao; her miraculous recovery from a 2016 accident motivated the temple construction) Manepally Murali Krishna (son of Sri Manepally Rama Rao; trustee) Manepally Sri Latha (daughter-in-law / trustee) Manepally Gopi Krishna (son / trustee) Manepally Mamatha (daughter-in-law / trustee) legends: In 2016, Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi had a life-threatening escalator accident, broke her bones, and was pushed into a coma. Doctors gave up, but tirtham (holy water) brought from Tirupati brought her back to life. The Manepally family then decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara as a way of thanksgiving and to celebrate the miracle. Construction began in 2018, and after over six years of work, the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy. The temple was designed to follow the Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya traditions, with each ritual — from the foundation stone to the final installation of the deity — adhering to ancient Agama Shastra traditions. The temple is named 'Swarnagiri' (Golden Hill) to reflect the inner radiance and spiritual wealth it aims to bestow upon visitors.

text: Swarnagiri Temple does not have a traditional ancient Sthala Puranam because it is a modern temple — built between 2018 and 2024 and consecrated only in 2024. The site's sacred character is derived from: (1) The Manepally family's personal miracle in 2016 (recovery of Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi from a coma after tirtham from Tirupati), which inspired the temple construction; (2) The temple's dedication to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, whose main idol is a 12-foot black-granite statue (the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana); (3) The Prana Pratishtha and Kumbhabhishekam performed by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy in March 2024 — which infuses the hilltop with divine energy and authentic Sri Vaishnava Agama sanctity; (4) The 108 steps symbolising the spiritual climb to the sanctum; (5) The 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second largest temple bell); and (6) The hilltop location (Manepally / Swarnagiri Hills) overlooking the historic Bhongir landscape — chosen for its picturesque setting that enhances the spiritual experience.

text: Devotees believe that praying to Lord Venkateswara at Swarnagiri brings financial stability, career success, and fulfilment of wishes. The 12-foot black-granite idol is considered especially powerful because of the Agama Shastra rituals performed at consecration and the daily pancha-samskara rituals. The illuminated Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi (water-filled sanctum) is a unique feature that gives visitors a meditative experience in the evening. The 40-foot monolithic Hanuman is venerated for protection, courage, and removal of obstacles. The 108 steps symbolise the spiritual ascent to the divine. The 1.5-ton bronze bell is rung during aarti and is said to carry prayers to the divine. Many devotees also visit Swarnagiri as part of the Yadadri temple circuit (Yadadri + Swarnagiri + Bhongir Fort + Kolanupaka Jain Temple) for a half-day spiritual trip from Hyderabad.

text: Swarnagiri Temple is a modern masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, drawing inspiration from the Pallava, Chola, Chalukya, and Vijayanagara styles. The temple complex is spread across 22 acres atop the Manepally Hills. The architecture features: (1) Four majestic Rajagopurams (temple gateways) on four sides of the prakara (outer wall), each adorned with intricate carvings and sacred patterns; (2) A five-storied Vimana Gopuram rising above the sanctum sanctorum (Garbha Griha); (3) The Garbha Griha houses a 12-foot-tall black-granite idol of Lord Venkateswara Swamy (the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana) — flanked by Goddesses Sridevi and Bhu Devi; (4) A 40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue (with a 27-foot Anjaneya as per the Telugu Wikipedia) and a massive 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest); (5) A spacious pradakshina path and well-planned mandapams (Maha Mandapam, Kalyana Mandapam, Yagasala); (6) The Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi — an illuminated water-filled sanctum that is a visual highlight in the evenings; (7) Sub-shrines of Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi; (8) A 40-foot tall Ratham (chariot) per the Telugu Wikipedia; (9) 108 steps leading from the foothills to the temple complex; (10) A Garuda Sthambham and a Pushkarini (sacred tank) with Vedic scholars' idols.

text:
Question: What is Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam?
Answer: Swarnagiri is a modern Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, located atop the scenic Manepally Hills in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana — about 47 km from Hyderabad. Built by the Manepally family (Manepally Charitable Trust / Srivari Seva Trust) on 22 acres of their own land, it was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy, following Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya. The temple features a 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest), and a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi.

text:
Question: Where is Swarnagiri Temple located?
Answer: Swarnagiri is on the Manepally Hills (Swarnagiri Hills) in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana – 508116, India. It is ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive), ~10 km from Bhuvanagiri town, ~15–18 km from Yadadri / Yadagirigutta, ~20 km from Surendrapuri, and ~35 km from Kolanupaka Jain Temple. The nearest railway station is Bhongir (~10 km) or Yadadri (~18 km). The nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km).

text:
Question: Who founded Swarnagiri Temple?
Answer: Swarnagiri was built by the Manepally family, led by Sri Manepally Rama Rao (a prominent businessman and philanthropist) along with his two sons, trustees Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi, Manepally Murali Krishna, Manepally Sri Latha, Manepally Gopi Krishna, and Manepally Mamatha. The temple was constructed under the Manepally Charitable Trust (also called the Srivari Seva Trust, established 30 January 2024). The idea of building the temple came from a deeply personal miracle in 2016, when Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi recovered from a life-threatening escalator accident and coma after tirtham (holy water) from Tirupati was brought to her. The family, in thanksgiving, decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara. Construction began in 2018, and the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy.

text:
Question: What is the architecture of Swarnagiri Temple?
Answer: Swarnagiri is a modern masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, drawing inspiration from the Pallava, Chola, Chalukya, and Vijayanagara styles. The temple complex is spread across 22 acres atop the Manepally Hills. Key architectural features include: (1) Four majestic Rajagopurams (temple gateways) on four sides of the prakara; (2) A five-storied Vimana Gopuram rising above the Garbha Griha; (3) The Garbha Griha houses a 12-foot black-granite idol of Lord Venkateswara (the largest in Telangana), flanked by Sridevi and Bhu Devi; (4) A 40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue; (5) A 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest); (6) A water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi (illuminated visual highlight in evenings); (7) Sub-shrines of Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi; (8) 108 steps leading up to the temple complex; (9) A 40-foot Ratham (chariot); and (10) A Pushkarini (sacred tank) with Vedic scholars' (Veda Murthis) idols.

text:
Question: What are the most important festivals at Swarnagiri?
Answer: The most important festival is Brahmotsavam — a 10-day grand celebration held annually between March and April (similar to the Tirumala Brahmotsavam). Other major festivals include Vaikunta Ekadashi (Dec/Jan), Rathasapthami, Sri Rama Navami, Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Hanuman Jayanti (March/April), Deepavali, and Vinayaka Chavithi (Ganesh Chaturthi) with Navaratri celebrations. During festivals, darshan timings are extended, special sevas are performed, and footfall exceeds 1 lakh.

Question: How much time do I need at Swarnagiri?
Answer: Plan to spend at least half a day to fully explore Swarnagiri. The temple has a sprawling 22-acre complex with multiple sub-shrines. Most visitors combine Swarnagiri with Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (~15–18 km), Bhongir Fort (~10 km), Surendrapuri (~20 km), and Kolanupaka Jain Temple (~35 km) for a full-day pilgrimage circuit from Hyderabad.

text:
Question: How do I reach Swarnagiri Temple from Hyderabad?
Answer: By road: ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive). Take NH 163 (Uppal → Ghatkesar → Bhongir → Swarnagiri) or the ORR Warangal NH 163 via the Ghatkesar exit. By bus: TGSRTC operates special buses from MGBS (Mahatma Gandhi Bus Stand) and JBS (Jubilee Bus Stand) to Yadadri (57 km and 55.8 km respectively), with onward connection to Swarnagiri. By train: nearest railway station is Bhongir (~10 km) or Yadadri (~18 km). Direct trains from Secunderabad to Yadadri: Krishna Express (17406), SC-WL (746), SC BDCR EXP (17659), HYB KZJ SPL (7758). By air: nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km).

text:
Question: What is the dress code at Swarnagiri Temple?
Answer: Swarnagiri Temple follows a simple and traditional dress code that aligns with Vaishnava temple customs. For men: dhoti-kurta, pancha, or formal pants paired with a shirt are appropriate. For women: saree, salwar kameez, churidar, or long skirt with dupatta. Traditional attire is especially recommended during special sevas or festive occasions. Avoid shorts, sleeveless tops, mini skirts, ripped jeans, or any revealing outfits inside the temple premises. Maintain proper dress and decorum to preserve the sanctity of the temple.

Question: Is Swarnagiri Temple accessible for elderly and disabled visitors?
Answer: Yes — Swarnagiri is wheelchair-accessible at the entrance and exit (per JustDial). Lifts are available for senior citizens and those unable to climb the 108 steps (per bloggymaster.com). Free Mahaprasad is distributed from 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM daily. There is ample parking at the foot of the hill. Photography is restricted inside the temple (cameras and mobile phones not allowed). Switch off your mobile phones at the temples; don't carry weapons or head gear (helmets, caps, turbans) inside the temple premises. Smoking and alcohol consumption are prohibited.
